Confirm with your master password. So nobody who has the unlocked app in hand for a moment can weaken the protection.
GhulSuite then stays unlocked when the screen goes off or Windows is locked.
Shaking then no longer locks at once.

The instant lock then leaves the event reminders on the device.

Format: CSV (title, user name, password, URL, notes), readable e.g. by Bitwarden, KeePassXC and Proton Pass.
Format: one otpauth line per account, readable by most authenticator apps.
The file contains all passwords or 2FA secrets in plain text. Anyone who gets it can read them. Use it only to move to another app and delete it afterwards.

Only for opening in Excel or LibreOffice: values starting with = + - or @ get an apostrophe in front, so they do not run as a formula. Leave it off for moving to another password manager, or the apostrophe ends up in the password.
Open the vault once with its previous password and its key or key file.
The copy in your suite is switched to your password, your keys and your recovery code. The original file stays as it is and still opens with its previous password: delete it if you no longer need it.
Delete the export file afterwards. It is not encrypted.

Supported: Proton Pass (ZIP, JSON, CSV), Bitwarden (JSON, CSV), KeePass/KeePassXC and other CSV files, Proton Authenticator, Aegis, 2FAS, otpauth links. Google Authenticator: scan the export QR code in GhulAuth.
Also add 2FA codes from logins to GhulAuth
Create a matching vault in the options first.

Name of the key (e.g. “Key on keyring”)

resources.string: The file is copied to your storage location, and the new suite gets a recovery code of its own: a code that belonged to the file before does not open it. But whoever gave you the file knows the password and key file. Afterwards change the password and add a key or key file of your own.
No entries yet. Use + to add your first password.
Camera access is needed to scan QR codes. The image is processed only on this device.

Choose an app PIN with 8 to 12 digits, not your screen lock PIN and no date. It only works on this device and only for quick unlock. After 2 wrong attempts it is gone; then only password and second factor open the suite.
Applies to the suite and all vaults. Keys, key files and the recovery code stay valid.
This code is shown only now. Write it down or print it and keep it in a safe place. The old code opens nothing you save from now on; it still opens old copies of the suite file, so delete those.
For moving from Proton, Bitwarden, KeePass, Aegis, 2FAS or Google Authenticator.
What opens your suite: the password plus one of the keys or key files. The recovery code opens everything on its own. Keep it safe.
Lock when the screen turns off
A new recovery code is created. The previous one then opens nothing you save from now on; it still opens old copies of the suite file.

The lock button and the notification lock normally. Shaking and the tile “Lock GhulSuite” in the quick settings are an instant lock: they also remove fingerprint and app PIN unlock, after that only the master password and the second factor open it. Event reminders keep working, unless you let the instant lock delete them too (they come back with the next unlock). A short vibration confirms locking by shaking.
Instant lock also deletes the event reminders

Password and second factor (key or key file) are needed after a restart and after the validity ends; after that quick unlock works again. You set it up again after an instant lock, after 2 wrong app PINs, when fingerprints are changed, and after every change of the protection (password, key, key file).
No secure fingerprint sensor or no fingerprint set up on this device.
After unlocking with password and second factor, you can open GhulSuite with your fingerprint or an app PIN for a while.
Quick unlock must be set up again after the update: switch fingerprint or app PIN on again (with password and second factor).
If you cancel the fingerprint prompt, fingerprint unlock is off afterwards.
Each method stays valid as long as chosen when it was set up. Another duration sets it up again, with password and second factor.

“%1$s” will no longer open anything you save from now on. Together with the old password it still opens an old copy of the suite file: delete old copies. Your other keys, key files and the recovery sheet stay valid.
Screenshots and screen recordings may then contain your passwords and codes, and the app is visible in the app switcher. Only allow this if you really need it.
GhulPass: show user names in the list

Lost something (key, key file or recovery sheet)? Removing it, or a new recovery sheet, locks it out of the current suite. An old copy of the suite file still opens with what you lost, though, and shows the state of back then. So delete old copies, and change the passwords of important accounts if you fear someone has such a copy. At the next save GhulSuite overwrites the old file at the same place with zeros; on sticks and SSDs even that is not fully certain. Safest is to save the suite file to a freshly formatted stick afterwards.
From key to key file. Afterwards your keys open nothing any more.
From key file to key, with a backup (second key or new key file).
A key file needs no backup in the app. Its backup is a copy kept elsewhere, not on the stick of the suite file.
A key always needs a backup: a second key or a key file. Replacing swaps a factor: the old one is no longer valid afterwards.
First confirm your protection: master password and one of your current factors.
Plug in the new key and touch it when GhulSuite asks. If you just confirmed with a key, unplug that one first.
Unplug the new key and plug in the second one. Touch it when GhulSuite asks.
Create the new key file and save it somewhere only you have access to, apart from the suite file.
This key is registered already. Plug in a different key and try again.
The old factor is removed. It opens nothing you save from now on.
The old factors are removed. They open nothing you save from now on.
Done. Save the suite file now so it has the new protection.
Older copies of the suite file (backups, an old stick, versions in the cloud) still open with the old factor. Best delete them.
Confirm once more with your key: plug in your current key and touch it when GhulSuite asks. Then you go on with the new one.
Plug in your first key and touch it when GhulSuite asks.
Unplug the first key and plug in the second one.
Touch the second key when GhulSuite asks.
That is the same key as the first one. Unplug it, plug in the second key and try again.
GhulAuth: show next code shortly before expiry
All vaults here belong to your suite. Each can also be taken along and opened on its own: with your password and second factor or with the recovery code.
Measuring the speed of this device …
I have written down or printed the code
This code opens all your vaults on its own, even if password, key and key file are gone. It is part of every one of your files. Write it down or print it and keep it safe, not on this device.
To be sure you have the code right, type in the whole code, best from your emergency sheet (spaces and dashes do not matter). GhulSuite compares every character.
That is not the code. Compare your emergency sheet with the code, character by character (with “Back”).
Please enter your key's PIN. If the key has none yet, tap "Check key" to set one.
On Windows you always unlock with password and key or key file; there is no quick unlock there.
With two keys: when setting this up asks for a touch, use your first key (“%1$s”), not the backup key. Its PIN is the one you entered first.
Your key has no PIN yet. GhulSuite requires one. Choose it now.
This password is too easy to guess. Use a longer one or several words.
A small file you keep apart from the suite file, e.g. on a stick of its own, not on the phone with the app. Good to start with; later you can swap it for a key.
A small file you keep safe

You need: this sheet, the suite file (%1$s, e.g. on the USB stick) and an Android phone or a Windows PC with the app GhulSuite (free at www.ghulsuite.de). The phone alone is not enough: the data is in the suite file.
%1$s (the suggested name, unless you chose another one when saving)
This recovery code opens your suite (suite file %1$s) completely, even without master password, security key and key file. Keep this sheet as safe as cash, away from your devices and key.

Print it directly via USB or Wi-Fi Direct if possible. Network and cloud printers may keep print jobs, and on Android the sheet goes through the printer maker’s print app, which is another app. “Save as PDF” puts the code into a file (usually in “Downloads”): delete it after printing. Copying it by hand is safest.
Open GhulSuite, choose “Open with emergency sheet” on the start screen and pick the suite file. If the suite is already set up on the device: “Locked out? Use recovery code” on the lock screen.
Enter this code (dashes and upper/lower case do not matter) and set a new master password.
In the options, add a new key or key file and remove lost ones before GhulSuite locks again.
Create a new recovery code and destroy this sheet.
Anyone with this sheet and your vault files can access all your data. Do not photograph it, do not store it in the cloud.
This is a file from inside a suite. Choose “Open suite file” and then the suite file (.ghlzip).
New suite with master password and security key or key file.
A saved suite (.ghlzip), e.g. from a USB stick.
A single vault file (.ghlpss, .ghltotp, .ghlcal and others) or a GhulDocs package (.ghldocs). Open only this vault, or add it to your suite.
Password or key lost: open the suite file with the recovery code from the emergency sheet.
There already are GhulSuite files here.
The code opens everything. Then set a new master password. Until it locks, it alone lets you replace lost factors.
Enter the recovery code from your emergency sheet.
Use password and key or key file

A .ghlpss or .ghltotp file, a GhulDocs package (.ghldocs) or a .ghlcal file: it becomes a vault of its own in your suite. If it has another password, you are asked for it once and it is switched to your protection.
The new vault gets your password, keys and recovery code and is stored as a separate file in your suite.
There is no vault for this area yet.
The vault is deleted from your suite, with all its entries.
Tip: export first what you want to keep.
The server certificate is not trusted (%1$s).
Windows asks for the PIN of your security key and for the touch in its own window.
Quick lock: the lock symbol, or Ctrl+L.
Show the QR code on the screen (e.g. in the browser), then scan. Or copy a picture of it.
Tap copies the code. Long press: rename, delete.
Insert your security key and touch it …
Passwords, 2FA, documents and calendar: encrypted on your devices, without a server.
No account, no cloud lock-in. A recovery code and an emergency sheet always come with it.
Scan with another device’s camera to join the Wi-Fi without typing. Nothing goes over the network.
The last 10 passwords stay encrypted in the entry. Handy if a change on the website did not work.
Attachments (up to 10 MB each) are stored encrypted in the vault and saved with it in the suite file.
Some tidying up is worth it
Everything is checked on this device only.
No one-time code in the entry or in GhulAuth
None of your passwords appears in known data breaches.
Via “Have I Been Pwned” with k-anonymity: only 5 characters of a hash leave the device.
Random words plus a number: easy to type, hard to guess (EFF word list).
Whoever sees this code can create your one-time codes. Only scan it to move to another app.
With this key any device makes the 2FA codes of this account. Whoever copies or photographs it has the second factor.
No QR code found in the image.
With device and version, no vault contents
Contains only version, device type and the last crash report, no passwords or content. Nothing is sent by itself: copy it, share it (e.g. with your mail app) or save it, and send it to the developer.

Passwords, 2FA, documents and calendar, encrypted on your devices. Open source under AGPL-3.0.

Plug in your security key now
Waiting up to one minute. Touch it when it blinks.
No events. The day is yours.
No events in the next 60 days.

Invitations go out as an .ics file through another app, no calendar server, no attendee tracking.

To remove single occurrences, delete them in their own view.
Saved only encrypted in the calendar vault (.ghlcal). Reminders are scheduled by the device itself, no server, no permanent notification.
Links stay inside the suite: the event only remembers what it points to.
Just type: day, time, repetition and #calendar are recognised.

resources.string: On Windows, reminders come while GhulSuite runs, also locked or in the notification area. When the program is closed, they do not come. On the phone they always come.

Your new password applies right away. Three more steps in Options → Keys and key files, best before you lock: until then your new password is enough for them, afterwards it takes password and second factor again. 1. Add a new key or key file. A key needs a backup (a second key or a key file), otherwise the lost factor cannot be removed. 2. Remove the lost key or key file. Afterwards it opens nothing you save from now on. 3. Create a new recovery sheet. The old one then opens nothing you save from now on; delete old copies of the suite file.
Opened with the recovery sheet: replace lost keys and create a new recovery sheet before you lock. Until then your new password is enough. Tap to open keys and key files.
What you entered here is not saved yet.
An edit was not saved when the app locked. It was discarded.
Create a calendar first, then you can import events.
"Export" takes all calendars, also hidden ones. A single calendar is exported in its settings.
Every calendar is stored encrypted in your suite (.ghlcal) and goes with the suite file like your passwords. Deliberately without CalDAV.
Built in and offline, nothing is looked up online.
“Event in 15 minutes”, without title and place

When you unlock, the device plans the reminders of the next 30 days itself (Android: exact alarms, Windows: while GhulSuite runs). They come on time, also while the app is locked, without a server and without a permanent notification. If you do not unlock for 28 days, GhulSuite reminds you to open the app; events after that are planned at the next unlock.
Colours, visibility, import and export of .ics files from Google, Outlook, Apple or Thunderbird.
GhulCal speaks no CalDAV and subscribes to no foreign calendars. Events travel encrypted in the suite file; only when you share an event or export it as .ics does it leave the device unencrypted.
Open GhulSuite so your event reminders keep coming.
As an .ics file, readable by any calendar program.
This file was made by a newer GhulSuite. Please update the app.
This file was made by an older development version of GhulSuite. Its format is not supported any more.
The suite is made on this device now. In the last step you create it as a suite file (.ghlzip) at a place you choose, e.g. on a USB stick.
The password never leaves your device. Without password and second factor only the recovery code helps (step 7).
Recommended · YubiKey, Nitrokey … via USB or NFC
Plug in the key and touch it when GhulSuite asks (when the suite is made in step 3).
No backup needed: keep a copy of the file elsewhere, not on the stick of the suite file.
To unlock you always need the password and this second factor. You can replace it later in Options.
Next, GhulSuite creates the suite. Touch your key twice when asked.
Every chosen area gets its own file with its settings. Areas not chosen create no file and are hidden. Switch them on any time in Options → Areas.
When GhulSuite is in the background or you do nothing.
Shake = instant lock: locks at once and deletes the quick unlock (fingerprint, PIN).
Everything can be changed later in Options → Locking. Applies to this device only.
Quick unlock means: with your fingerprint or an app PIN instead of password and second factor (key or key file), for the time between two full unlocks.
The app PIN needs 8 to 12 digits.
Then password and second factor again.
No expiry. After a restart of the device, an instant lock or a password change you still need password and second factor again.

%1$s. The file %2$s is created and saved in the suite file like everything else.
Accounts and favourites live in the vault, so there is nothing else to set here.
Your recovery code was never confirmed.

The setup was interrupted. Unlock with your password and second factor, then GhulSuite completes the suite.

stays in its login, only not in GhulAuth
With the original data, in the folder “%1$s”, nothing gets lost. You can take it over by hand later.

Only released versions. Checked at most once a day after unlocking; nothing is installed without asking you.

Program and settings are on the stick here, without a seal. Whoever had the stick for a while can swap the program and read password and second factor at the next unlock. Do not start GhulSuite from a stick that was out of your hands: download the portable version again from the release page and check its checksum (SHA256SUMS).
Allow “Install unknown apps” for GhulSuite once, then tap “Install” again.

Emergency: the code opens the file without the password. Its seal cannot be checked then. Afterwards a new master password protects the suite.
This replaces the suite on this device. Confirm with its master password and key or key file, or with its recovery code.
Opened with the recovery code: save the suite at a new place. The opened file stays as it was.
This file holds another suite than the one on this device. It replaces everything here.
This file is older than your state here.
This file was carried on from another state than yours here.
This device has changes that are in no suite file yet. They are lost. Save first if you want to keep them.
Opened with the recovery code: without the password it could not be checked that the file is unchanged.

This suite file is incomplete: saving was probably interrupted (stick pulled, app ended). The state in the app is not affected; save it again, best at a new place. If you have an older copy, open that one.
Parts of the suite file do not match its list: it was changed or is damaged.
A newer state was built meanwhile. Please save again.
%1$s is a %2$s vault. What would you like to do?
Only this vault is unlocked, your suite stays locked. Changes go straight back into this file.
After you unlock your suite, the vault is added to it and gets the protection of your suite.
Start a new suite with it
%1$s (%2$s). Enter the password of the vault and its key or key file.
Open on its own: %1$s from %2$s. Your suite stays locked. Every change is written back into this file.
Writing the changes into the file …
The file could not be written (is the storage still there?). Your changes are still here.
Closing or locking ends it; changes not yet written go into the file first.
Second factor of the new vault:
To confirm: your own suite, with master password and key or key file.
Last step: save the vault file.
Now save the new key file. Hand it over separately from the vault file.
The recovery code of the new vault. It opens the vault without password and key: hand it over separately or keep it safe. It is shown only now.
After unlocking, %1$s is added to your suite.
Choose either a new key file or a security key.
No vault is open on its own.
Only GhulPass and GhulAuth entries can be shared as a separate vault.
The master password is too short: it needs at least 10 characters.
The master password is too easy to guess. Choose a longer one, e.g. several words with numbers.
The suite on this device is only replaced when you confirm it with its master password and key or key file, or its recovery code.
Something changed on this device since the file was checked. Open the file again.
An earlier opening of a suite file could not be finished. Restart the app. If it stays, free some space and close other programs that might use the files of GhulSuite.

An earlier save was not finished, and the state before it cannot be put back right now. Free some space, close other programs that might use the files of GhulSuite and unlock again. Do not delete the suite.
Only a security key over USB or NFC can be added; a phone or a Bluetooth device does not work.
The vault could not be removed: its file cannot be deleted right now. Close other programs that may have it open and try again.

The documents from before the last opening of a suite file were not found. So that nothing is lost, everything stays as it is. Restart the app and check that its data folder is all there (is the stick plugged in properly, for example?).
Documents are being added or copied right now. Try again when that is done.
Folders cannot be nested any deeper.
This GhulDocs vault already has as many folders as it can hold.
The file holds too many events (at most 20,000 at once).
Choose how long quick unlock should stay valid.

The app may not write into this file (e.g. a mail attachment, or another app handed it over without the right to write). Choose it in GhulSuite itself with “Open”, save it somewhere else first, or add the vault to your suite.
Done. Give the vault file, the password and, if there is one, the key file separately; the recipient keeps the recovery code safe.
The last changes to %1$s could not be written into its file (was the storage gone, or the app ended?). Write them now, or give them up.
Still not written. Is the storage there? Try again later.
Not while a vault is open on its own.
A vault of the suite cannot be read (Options → Vaults). Remove it or bring it back, then save.
The file was changed elsewhere since it was opened. Overwrite it with this vault, or save this vault as a new file.
The file was changed elsewhere meanwhile: writing would overwrite that. Save as a new file instead if unsure.
The last changes to %1$s are lost; the file stays as it is.
%1$s was changed since or cannot be read (was writing it cut off?). Giving up may lose this vault. Better save it as a new file.
Changes of the last opening still wait for this file. Write them first (or give them up).
The vault is still being written into its file. Try again in a moment.
Changes of a vault opened on its own are left, but which file they belong to is unreadable. Save them as a new file, or give them up.
The file is gone or cannot be read (moved, deleted, storage away?). Write it anew there, or save as a new file.
The file is not there or cannot be read now. Writing creates it anew.
These changes are lost; which file they belonged to is unknown.
The file is gone or cannot be read (moved, deleted, storage away?). It is written as soon as it is back; else save the vault as a new file.
%1$s is not there now. If it is really gone, giving up loses this vault. Better save it as a new file.
The file is not there or cannot be read now. Is the storage back? Then try again; otherwise save as a new file.
Still not there. Is the storage back? Otherwise save as a new file.

The protection of your suite was changed. Save the suite file now and replace older copies on other devices, sticks or in backups with it. Older copies still open with the old protection: delete them. Until you save, the older file is your only copy, so everything stays as it was until then.
Important documents and scans, up to 1 GB per vault
This GhulDocs vault is full: %1$s of %2$s used. Nothing was added. Empty the trash, delete documents or create another GhulDocs vault.
This file is too large for GhulDocs (at most %1$s per vault). It was not added.
What is in the trash still counts towards the limit of 1 GB per vault until the trash is emptied.
Everything in the trash is deleted for good. This cannot be undone.
This folder is empty. Add files with “Add”.
No favourites yet. Mark a document with the star.
No GhulDocs vault yet. Create one under Options → Vaults.
Encrypted on this device. Names, folders and contents are only in the vault.
This GhulDocs vault is almost full.
From this device, several at once
With the camera, several pages into one PDF
To scan documents GhulSuite needs the camera. The photos stay in the memory of this device and are never saved unencrypted.
The camera could not be started.
Hold the sheet flat in the picture, on a dark surface if you can.
Drag the four corners onto the corners of the sheet.
Gray with more contrast, for text
Many pages: the memory of the phone may run short. Save the PDF soon.
Not enough memory for another page. Save the pages taken so far first.
The photo could not be taken. Try again.
The page could not be processed. Try again.
Photos and pages are only in memory and are gone when you leave the scan or lock the app. Only the finished PDF is saved, encrypted.
Adding %1$s cancelled. Nothing of it was kept.
“%1$s” from another app, encrypted in GhulDocs.

%1$s files from another app, encrypted in GhulDocs.

resources.string: Files shared with GhulSuite go into GhulDocs: set it up first (Options, Areas).
A temporary copy, deleted when GhulSuite locks
Saved unencrypted at a place you choose
“%1$s” is saved without encryption at the place you choose next. Anyone with access to that place can read it.
Export of %1$s cancelled. The incomplete file was removed.
No program to open it was found.

“Open with app” hands a temporary copy to the app you choose; it is removed when GhulSuite locks. What that app does with it is up to that app. Programs, scripts and shortcuts are not opened this way.
Also in the portable version this copy lies in the temp folder of this PC, not on the stick. Removed does not mean securely erased: SSDs and sticks can keep remnants.
GhulSuite does not open files of the type .%1$s with another app: they can start programs or run content. If you trust the file, export it and check it first.
Archives can hold programs. Only open what you expect in it, and do not start programs from it that you do not trust.

The copy could not be marked as coming from the internet (the temp folder is on a drive without this mark). Without it Windows would not warn about anything in it, so it is not opened. Export the document instead.
The app cannot show this type of file.
Too large to show in the app (more than %1$s).
This PDF cannot be shown here (protected by a password or damaged).
This image cannot be shown here.
Open it with another app or export it.
Only the beginning of the text is shown.
A GhulDocs vault holds up to 1 GB, the trash included, a single file also up to 1 GB. A suite has up to 3 GhulDocs vaults (3 GB and 20,000 documents together).
Reads every document of a vault and compares it with its checksum. Nothing is changed.
Open an earlier suite file to get them back.

%1$s items in the trash, in all GhulDocs vaults.

%1$s selected items go into a GhulDocs package of its own (a .ghldocs file with the documents), with a password, second factor and recovery code of its own. Nothing of your suite's protection goes with it.

resources.string: To keep it in a suite of its own: set up a new suite first, then add this file under Options, Vaults.
The last changes of the GhulDocs vault in %1$s could not be written into its file before it was locked. A GhulDocs vault can only be written while it is open: give them up to open the file again.
Open the GhulDocs package once with its own password and its key or key file. It then becomes a GhulDocs vault of its own in your suite, with its documents, and gets your suite's protection.
The file needs %1$s, %2$s are free in this GhulDocs vault. Nothing was added. Empty the trash, delete documents or use another GhulDocs vault.
This needs %1$s, %2$s are free in this GhulDocs vault. Nothing was added. Empty the trash, delete documents or use another GhulDocs vault.
The package needs %1$s, a GhulDocs vault holds at most %2$s. Nothing was added.
There already is a suite on this device. Choose what happens to it.
The new suite is not set up.
Save the existing suite and replace it
Save it as a file (.ghlzip) first, then delete it and set up the new one
Delete the existing suite and replace it
Without saving: its data is then gone for good

Unlock the existing suite with its master password and its key or key file. Then choose where the file (.ghlzip) is saved. Only once it is written and checked, the existing suite is deleted on this device and the new one is set up.
Unlocked. Now choose where the file is saved.
The file was not written completely. Nothing was deleted.
This file belongs to another suite or holds another state. Choose a new name so nothing is overwritten. Nothing was deleted.
Saved as %1$s. Deleting the existing suite was not confirmed; the file stays its place.
The existing suite is saved. Confirm deleting it with its master password and key or key file.
Delete the existing suite for good?
Everything of the existing suite on this device is deleted for good: all vaults (passwords, 2FA, documents in GhulDocs, calendars) and the quick unlock.
A suite file (.ghlzip) saved somewhere else is not touched. If you have not saved the suite as a file yet, better choose “Save the existing suite and replace it”.
To delete it you need the existing suite: its master password with key or key file, or its recovery code.

If you have neither the password with key or key file nor the code, or the suite here cannot be read any more: clear the app storage in the Android settings under Apps → GhulSuite. Then everything of GhulSuite on this device is gone; suite files elsewhere stay.

If you have neither the password with key or key file nor the code, or the suite here cannot be read any more: quit GhulSuite and delete the folder %1$s. Then everything of GhulSuite on this PC is gone; suite files elsewhere stay.
With password and key or key file
This needs %1$s, all GhulDocs vaults together have %2$s free (at most %3$s per suite). Nothing was added. Empty a trash or delete documents or a GhulDocs vault.
All GhulDocs vaults together are full: %1$s of %2$s used (at most 20,000 documents). Nothing was added. Empty a trash or delete documents or a GhulDocs vault.
For you, encrypted with your password and key or key file: as a backup or for another device
For someone else: with a password, key or key file and recovery code of its own
Under ⋮: "Export" saves the vault encrypted with your protection, for you. "Share as separate vault" is for someone else (with a password, second factor and recovery code of its own).

The whole vault "%1$s" goes into a new vault file with a password, second factor and recovery code of its own. Nothing of your suite's protection goes with it; from GhulPass, old passwords stay behind.

The whole GhulDocs vault "%1$s" goes with all its documents (not the trash) into a GhulDocs package of its own (.ghldocs), with a password, second factor and recovery code of its own. Nothing of your suite's protection goes with it.
All GhulDocs vaults together are almost full (at most 3 GB per suite).
A suite has at most 3 GhulDocs vaults (up to 1 GB each). Delete one to create a new one or add a GhulDocs package.
This file holds more GhulDocs vaults than a suite may have (at most 3) and is no valid suite file. It was not opened.
There are changes that are not in the suite file yet. Unlock and tap the save icon at the top.
Write the changes into the suite file now?
Never saved into a suite file yet.
There is no suite file yet. Choose where it should be, best on a USB stick in a folder of its own. Until then your data is on this device only.
While it is saved: do not pull the USB stick and keep the app open.
Checking the file at its place …
New changes came in meanwhile. They are not in the suite file yet.
The suite file at this place was saved on another device meanwhile. If you overwrite it, the changes from there are lost.
The suite file was saved elsewhere

The suite file %1$s was saved from another state meanwhile, usually on another device. Open it now, before you change anything here, or there will be two states. When opening, the app says whether it is newer or older.
The suite file %1$s was saved with a changed protection (e.g. a new password or a new recovery code on another device). Open it now, before you change anything here.
At this place there is another suite or a file that cannot be read (e.g. from a save that was cut off).
Save mine as a new file …
Not saved into the suite file since %1$s. Tap to save.
New or changed entries are only on this device, not yet in the suite file. Tap to save.
The suite file is still being saved (%1$s). Do not pull the USB stick.

Everything you change is on this device at once, encrypted (in the working copy). It gets into the suite file, your backup to take along, only when you save: tap the save icon at the top (on a PC also Ctrl+S). It shows as soon as something is unsaved. Save before you go on working on another device. Exporting and sharing do not replace saving.

Everything you change is on this device at once, encrypted. It gets into the suite file, your backup to take along (e.g. on a USB stick), only when you tap the save icon at the top. It shows as soon as something is unsaved. If this device is lost, only what was saved into the suite file is left. Input you have not applied yet is lost when the app locks.
There are changes that are not in the suite file yet. Save before quitting? Without saving they stay on this device and can be saved later.
There are changes that are not in the suite file yet. Unlock first to save them. Without saving they stay on this device and can be saved later.
The suite file is being saved right now (%1$s). The app quits as soon as saving is done.
Without a suite file your data is on this device only. If it is lost, everything is gone. Try again or choose another place; you can also create it later with the save icon at the top.

At this place the suite file would be written over directly at every save. Choose a safe place: a folder of its own (e.g. “GhulSuite”, create it in the picker). The app creates the suite file there anew; the one just saved stays where it is.

Saved. This place (e.g. a cloud app) only allows writing over the file directly: if a later save is interrupted, the file there is unusable. Cloud apps also keep older versions, even after deleting. A USB stick or a folder on the device is better.
Best on a USB stick or in the storage in a folder of its own (e.g. “GhulSuite”), which you can create in the picker. Not “Download” and not the top level: Android does not share those.
An entry is being edited and not applied yet. Apply it first and then save, or quit without it.
The suite file is being saved right now. The app quits as soon as saving is done.
The suite file is still being saved. Do not pull the USB stick.
Too many failed biometric attempts. Unlock with the master password and key or key file, or try again later.
Notifications are turned off for GhulSuite: reminders do not arrive.
Finish saving, adding or editing first, then update.
The update is being installed; the app ends in a moment. Save afterwards.
The last update was not installed (error %1$s). GhulSuite keeps running the old version; try again or get the update from the release page.
The last update was cancelled. GhulSuite keeps running the old version.
The last update was not installed: the file had another checksum after loading. Try again; if it happens again, get the update from the release page.
The last update was not installed: the file could not be checked before installing (PowerShell is missing or blocked). Get the update from the release page.
The update was not carried out, probably the virus protection stopped it. GhulSuite keeps running the old version. Get the update from the release page: github.com/ghulaschsuppe/GhulSuite/releases
The update needs Windows PowerShell, which could not be started. Get the update from the release page: github.com/ghulaschsuppe/GhulSuite/releases
A security key needs a backup: a second key or a key file. Add a backup first.
To confirm: master password and your key or key file. Whoever has the unlocked app in hand for a moment cannot change your protection this way.
Opened with the recovery code: until it locks, your new master password is enough. Replace lost factors now and create a new recovery code.
If your key gets lost, the backup still gets you in. It works just like the key: a key file (kept apart from the suite file, e.g. on a stick of its own) or a second security key.
You set up the second key right after the suite is made, step by step.
Your key has no backup. If it gets lost, only the recovery code gets you in. Add a second key or a key file.
The suite is made, but the backup is still missing. Try the second key again (touch the first one first) or take a key file instead.

The suite file at this place has a newer protection: on another device the password was changed, a key removed or a new recovery code made meanwhile. Overwriting would undo that (an old code would open it again), so it is not offered. If you open the file (with your current or the new password and key), the changes of this device that are not in it are lost.

To keep them: hand on every vault with changes from here as a file of its own under Options → Vaults → ⋮ “Share as separate vault” (own password and key file). Then open the new suite file and take the files back in with “Add vault file”. A new suite file from here is not offered for this: it would have the old protection, and an old recovery code would open it.
The app may not write back into this file. Use \u201cSave as\u201d to save to a place of your choice.
This file came from another app. Should GhulSuite save here from now on? Only if you put it there yourself; otherwise save with “Save as” to a place you choose.
This app does not let GhulSuite keep writing to the file. Save with “Save as” to a place you choose.
%1$s is on a network drive and is not opened by double click while GhulSuite runs. Open it in GhulSuite with “Open suite file”.

Here the app can only write over the suite file directly. So that saving never leaves half a file, choose a safe place once: a folder of its own (e.g. “GhulSuite”, create it in the picker). The app creates the suite file there anew; the old one stays where it is.
Android does not share this folder (“Download” or the top level). Choose a subfolder or create one, e.g. “GhulSuite”.
This folder belongs to another app (e.g. a cloud app) or could not be shared. Choose a folder in the device’s storage, on the SD card or a USB stick, or use “Save as”.
There is already a file GhulSuite.ghlzip in this folder. Choose another folder or create a new one.

The suite file is in the folder “Download” or at the top of the storage. Android does not share these places with any app, so the file is written over directly at every save. Choose a safe place once: a folder of its own (e.g. “GhulSuite”, create it in the picker). The app creates the suite file there anew; the old one stays where it is.

This place (e.g. a cloud app) does not allow swapping: the file there is written over directly. If that is interrupted, the file is unusable; your data then stays in the app. Cloud apps also keep older versions, even after deleting. A USB stick or a folder on the device is safer.

The suite file is written over directly. If saving is interrupted (stick pulled, app ended, cloud app failing), it is unusable and only the state in this app is left. Safer: save it as a new file next to it.
